Its si_dimension is L T^-1 and its dimension_vector is [0, 1, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0], which provides the full SI exponent set (I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=-1, Theta=0) claimed in before_si_exponents; thus all coordinates are supported by this KB record.

The ledger labels nu as kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity). The pq_kinematic_viscosity record defines kinematic viscosity (ν) as dynamic viscosity divided by density and gives si_dimension L^2 T^-1 with dimension_vector [0, 2, -1, 0, 0, 0, 0]. This entry therefore directly corresponds to the problem’s nu and confirms each SI exponent (I=0, J=0, L=2, M=0, N=0, T=-1, Theta=0) listed in before_si_exponents.

The problem describes MKE as the integral of the square of the local mean flow speed with respect to wall-normal distance (integral U^2 dy). The pq_integrated_velocity_squared record defines exactly that integrated mean-flow-squared-velocity measure and states dimensions follow from U^2 times length, i.e. si_dimension L^3 T^-2 with dimension_vector [0, 3, -2, 0, 0, 0, 0]. That KB entry thus matches the ledger’s MKE definition and supports the full SI exponent vector given in before_si_exponents.

The pq_boundary_layer_thickness record explicitly names boundary-layer thickness with symbols delta, δ, delta99, δ99 and the operational definition ‘99-percent free-stream-velocity thickness’; its si_dimension is L with dimension_vector [0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. This directly corresponds to the ledger’s delta and supports all SI exponents (I=0, J=0, L=1, M=0, N=0, T=0, Theta=0).

The ledger identifies delta* as the boundary-layer displacement thickness. The pq_displacement_thickness record defines displacement thickness (δ*) as the integral boundary-layer thickness representing the mass-flow deficit relative to the external flow, with si_dimension L and dimension_vector [0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. That KB record therefore directly applies to the ledger’s delta* and supports the SI exponents listed in before_si_exponents.

The ledger names theta as the boundary-layer momentum thickness. The pq_momentum_thickness entry defines momentum thickness (θ) as the integral thickness representing the momentum deficit and gives si_dimension L with dimension_vector [0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. This entry matches the ledger’s theta and fully supports the SI exponents in before_si_exponents.

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: U_tau/U_inf is dimensionless. The six input quantities span only the base dimensions of length (L) and time (T); mass, electric current, temperature, amount, and luminous intensity do not appear. By Buckingham Pi, with 6 variables and 2 fundamental dimensions, there are 6-2 = 4 independent dimensionless groups. Natural choices are: Re_delta = U_inf * delta / nu (Reynolds number based on delta); Pi_MKE = MKE/(U_inf^2 * delta) (dimensionless integral of mean kinetic energy normalized by U_inf^2 * delta); Pi_delta_star = delta*/delta; Pi_theta = theta/delta. Therefore U_tau/U_inf = F(Re_delta, Pi_MKE, Pi_delta_star, Pi_theta). All input exponents are known with high confidence from their definitions.
